subject: physics
title: Charge and current
key_idea: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge. Charge flows only in a closed circuit that includes a source of potential difference. Charge flow = current × time.

blocks.text: Current is a flow of electrical charge. In a metal wire the charge that flows is made of electrons.

items.meaning: The rate of flow of electrical charge. Measured in amperes (A).
The amount of charge that passes a point. Measured in coulombs (C).

items: The circuit must include a **source of potential difference**, such as a cell, battery or power supply.
The circuit must be a **closed circuit**, with no gaps, so the charge has a complete path.
If either is missing, there is no current in the circuit.
A current has the same value at any point in a single closed loop.
An ammeter placed before a lamp and one placed after it show the same reading.
Components do not use up current. They transfer energy.
Current is the rate of flow of charge. In metals, the charge is carried by electrons.
Charge flows only with a source of potential difference and a closed circuit.
The current is the same everywhere in a single closed loop.

blocks.text: Charge flow, current and time are linked by one equation. Use it for any current that stays steady.
Rearrange the equation to find current or time.

items: Time must be in **seconds**. Multiply minutes by 60 and hours by 3600.
Current must be in **amperes**. Divide milliamperes (mA) by 1000.
Forgetting to convert is the most common way to lose marks in this calculation.

items.text: A current of 15 A flows for 2 minutes. t = 2 × 60 = 120 s.

diagram.alt: Calculate the charge flow from a current and a time, with new numbers each time.
diagram.question: A current of {I} A flows in a wire for {t} seconds. Calculate the charge flow.

items: Convert minutes to seconds and milliamperes to amperes before substituting.

checks.q: State the two conditions needed for charge to flow in a circuit.
checks.a: A source of potential difference and a closed (complete) circuit.

checks.q: A current of 2.5 A flows for 30 seconds. Calculate the charge that flows.
A current of 40 mA transfers a charge of 3.6 C. Calculate how long this takes.

mistakes.right: Time must be in seconds, so 5 minutes is 300 s. A correct substitution with an unconverted time can score some marks, but the answer is wrong.

mistakes.wrong: The charge flow through a lamp with a current of 200 mA is 200 × 15 = 3000 C.
mistakes.right: Convert the current first: 200 mA = 0.2 A. Then charge flow = 0.2 × 15 = 3.0 C.

mistakes.wrong: Electrical current is a flow of energy.
mistakes.right: Electrical current is a flow of charge.

worked_example.question:
The battery supplies a current of 130 000 A.

Calculate the charge flow from the battery in 5 minutes.

Choose the unit from the box.

coulombs   newtons   watts

Charge flow = ______ Unit ______
worked_example.tip: One mark for converting the time, one for the substitution, one for the answer and one for the unit.

mistakes.wrong: The current in the lamp is a flow of ions.
mistakes.right: In a metal conductor the current is a flow of electrons.

mistakes.wrong: Charge = 2.5 × 8 = 20 C for 8 minutes at 2.5 A.
mistakes.right: Convert 8 minutes to seconds: 2.5 × 8 × 60 = 1200 C. The unconverted answer of 20 C scores 1 mark only.

mistakes.wrong: The answer is 63 with no unit.
mistakes.right: The unit is a separate mark. Write 63 coulombs, or 63 C.

worked_example.question:
The current in a lamp is 0.21 A.

Calculate the charge that flows through the lamp in a time of 300 s.
State the unit of charge.

Use the equation
charge = current × time
worked_example.tip: The unit is an independent mark. C, c and As are all accepted.

exam_phrases: Charge flow = current × time / Q = It
Conversion of mA to A (40 mA = 0.04 A)

mistakes.wrong: The conditions for charge to flow are ions and charge.
mistakes.right: Ions and charge are ignored. Write potential difference (or voltage) and a closed or complete circuit.

mistakes.wrong: Q = 15 × 2 = 30 C for 15 A for 2 minutes.
mistakes.right: The time was not converted. Use 2 × 60 = 120 s, so Q = 15 × 120 = 1800 C.

mistakes.wrong: A current of 40 mA takes 3.6 ÷ 40 = 0.09 s to transfer 3.6 C.
mistakes.right: Convert mA to A first: 40 mA = 0.04 A. Then t = 3.6 ÷ 0.04 = 90 s.

worked_example.question:
Calculate the charge flow in a circuit when there is a current of 15 A for 2 minutes.

Use the equation: charge flow = current × time

Charge flow = ______ C
worked_example.tip: Check the answer line first. 1800 C scores all 3 marks. 30 C, with the time not converted, scores 2 marks.
